title: Why MCP revenue is still zero
conclusion: The payment and distribution assets exist, but qualified buyer discovery and the reason to buy Pro remain unvalidated. Google delivered 0 measured clicks; hosted usage records 19 unmarked successful responses and 0 checkout handoffs.
accountability: Server counts, tests, directory listings, clones and synthetic probes are supply or reliability evidence. They are not sales, customers or demonstrated return on investment. The current server experiment is a bounded test of a documented workflow, not proof of demand.

findings.title: Qualified discovery remains the limiting evidence
findings.status: 38 Google impressions, 0 clicks; task URL rows retain their dated source
findings.evidence: Finalized 2026-09-26 through 2026-10-23; homepage and protocol routes receive the impressions. GitHub reports 83 views and 43 clients in its separate window.
findings.implication: Send existing relevant distribution traffic directly to an exact free task. Measure trials and repeat use before broad catalogue expansion.

findings.title: Some hosted protocol use is now visible
findings.evidence: The counters pool all servers. Source declarations are not verified attribution. There are 1612 unmarked offer views and 0 unmarked handoffs in the same seven-date instrument window.
findings.implication: Keep the useful free workflows and source attribution. Do not treat automation-inclusive counters as a person-level conversion funnel.

findings.title: Revenue is still unproven
findings.status: Zero paid MCP Checkout Sessions across available completed history
findings.evidence: Two exhausted pages contain 186 completed paid account records as positive controls; exact host, known price and metadata independently find no MCP paid match.
findings.implication: A tested payment path is necessary. Buyer willingness to pay and actual net ROI still require independent receipts and attributable costs.

findings.title: Separate dead-route clicks from unresolved navigation
findings.status: 4 known dead-route observations; 0 other guard-passing clicks
findings.evidence: The unknown-product branch returns HTTP 404 and preserves a valid supplied source label when present. Other source buckets alone cannot certify valid-product interest.
findings.implication: Preserve dead-link diagnostics separately and keep unresolved clicks unresolved. Do not present these observations as buyers considering Pro.

correction.title: The previous $38 MCP sales claim was incorrect
correction.text: The two referenced Stripe records are real paid $4.99 subscriptions on zovo.one, not $19 MCP purchases. Neither has an MCP price, product metadata or MCP line-item name. They do not validate MCP demand or MCP license fulfillment. The old note is retained with a prominent correction.

decision: Repair paid-access reliability, publish one narrow supplier-statement experiment with a useful free tier, and direct existing distribution to demonstrated workflows. Treat any expansion as an experiment until qualified repeat use and an independent payment are observed.

next_test.measure: Count an actual relevant operator with a supplied, permitted or redacted batch and an observed completed review. Exclude agents, crawlers, fixture data and directory accepts.
next_test.gate: 10 observed trials; diagnose installation and input friction for each failed attempt.

next_test.action: Test repeat use and the existing paid reason
next_test.measure: Ask why a user would return, whether more saved reports matters, and what prevents purchase. Record the answer; do not infer it from a click.
next_test.gate: 3 participants return with a second batch and at least 1 independent buyer pays the current offer. These are proposed decision thresholds, not forecasts.

next_test.measure: If 10 qualified users cannot be recruited, change the acquisition approach. If they try but do not return, change the workflow. If they return but do not pay, change the paid offer.
next_test.gate: No broad product expansion until buyer acquisition, repeat value and a paid outcome are observed. A week with too few trials is inconclusive, not product rejection.

limits: No person-level conversion rate or net-profit claim.
Historical audit and prior sprint files are preserved.
No outreach email or live purchase was created by this review.
Deployment, artifact tests and production observation are separately dated evidence.
